content.comment_body: Hello, Have you identified the issue? When I connect the slave module to the second [article_no], the [product_name] device changes its IP address to match the master device's IP. Is this expected? Because I can't use [product_name] software and my LAN encounters issues.
Hello [user_name], I recommend starting with a simple program. For reference, you can check this sample program: [url] If this doesn't resolve your issue, please upload your program here.
Thank you, it worked. Is it possible to access inputs beyond I8, such as I9 to I24?

Yes, it's possible to use up to 24 inputs on a [product_name] [article_no] slave module by adding two [product_name] expansion modules. However, keep in mind you can only use a total of 32 bits for slave inputs and outputs, for example, 24 inputs plus 8 outputs.

analysis.insight_summary: Users addressed a situation where adding a slave module on a second [article_no] caused the IP address of their [product_name] device to change to match the master's IP, resulting in LAN communication issues and making the [product_name] software inaccessible. An example program helped resolve the main problem. The conversation further clarified limitations on the number of usable inputs and outputs when connecting expansion modules to the [product_name] [article_no].
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to add slave modules to the [product_name] [article_no] without causing network conflicts or unwanted IP changes, and wants to be able to access more digital inputs beyond I8.
